newsitem.title: INDIA: India tax break applies to infrastructure firms.
newsitem.headline: India tax break applies to infrastructure firms.

text.p: The Indian government said on Thursday that an exemption from long-term capital gains tax which was announced on Wednesday applies to shares issued by publicly-traded companies involved in infrastructure work.

On Wednesday, the government released a statement saying President Shankar Dayal Sharma had issued an ordinance allowing investment in shares issued by public companies to be exempt from long-term capital gains tax. The statement did not specify which public companies were covered by the ordinance.
Krishna Saini, deputy secretary of the tax policy division in the Finance Ministry, told Reuters that public limited companies whose shares are widely traded are eligible to be covered.
To be eligible, a firm has to be engaged in infrastructure development including basic telephone services and extraction of oil and gas, Saini said.
Firms engaged in power generation or in power generation and distribution are also eligible, he said. Companies engaged only in power distribution are not covered, he said.
Saini said the government had issued a circular spelling out the tax exemption guidelines.
Private sector companies that want their shares to be covered by the exemption must apply to the Central Board of Direct Taxes, he said.
